newsitem.title: UK: British Airways launches recruitment drive.
newsitem.headline: British Airways launches recruitment drive.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Friday launched its drive to recruit 5,000 new staff under a previously-announced plan whereby around 5,000 BA staff are to take voluntary severance or early redundancy and others are to be hired "with different skills".
BA said in a statement it had planned to fill the vacancies over the next three years.
The 5,000 recruitments, which include last week's announcement of more than 700 new staff for London's Gatwick airport, is BA's biggest recruitment programme since the late 1980s.
"We work in an increasingly competitive industry and must continue to be the first choice in every major market which we serve," BA chief executive Bob Ayling said in the statement.
"The recruitment drive is a demonstration that our 'Change' programme is not just a cost-cutting exercise, but a positive story of investment," he said.
"Although there will be fewer jobs in some areas, this recruitment plan is proof that we envisage employing more people overall at the turn of the century than we do today," he said.
